subject: plumbing
intro: Plumbing leads to licensed pipe trades work: installing and repairing the systems that move clean water in and waste out, running projects as a contractor or manager, and operating the treatment plants that keep water safe.

roles.title: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
roles.what: Install and repair the piping systems that carry water, steam and waste through buildings: read plans, measure and cut pipe, fit fixtures and appliances, and test systems for leaks against code, usually after a four to five year apprenticeship.
roles.where: Every unit of this course is trade work — code and drawings for plan reading and inspection, water supply systems for pressure, sizing and backflow, and drain-waste-vent for slopes, traps and venting.

roles.title: Construction Managers
roles.what: Plan, coordinate and budget construction projects from start to finish: schedule the trades, monitor costs and quality, respond to delays and emergencies, and make sure work complies with building codes and other regulations.
roles.where: The permits and inspection topic, blueprint reading for plumbing, and the industry-structure discussion in unit one give you the vocabulary to coordinate plumbers among the other trades on site.

roles.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
roles.what: Operate the plants and pumping systems that treat water and wastewater: run pumps and valves, test samples, adjust chemical dosing, and keep treatment processes within safety and environmental standards.
roles.where: The potable water piping and pressure, sizing and backflow prevention topics teach how supply systems behave, and the greywater and sustainable systems unit introduces the reuse ideas treatment plants implement.
